messages:
prod-alerts-bot: :rotating_light: Alerts: 5xx rate spike and timeouts on /v1/generate across eu-west-1. p95 -> 1.4s (baseline ~0.18s), p99 -> 6.2s. Error rate 5xx ~ 4.8% (normally <0.1%). Deploy tag: release/2026-03-15-13:22 (canary promoted at 13:27). Correlation: increased gateway timeouts and downstream 502s.

emma (oncall-sre): saw the alert. pausing any non-essential deploys. can anyone confirm if the canary was promoted? what was the deploy id? @deploy-bot any info? :eyes:

deploy-bot: Canary promotion recorded for deploy_id=dep-20260315-1315, promoted to prod at 4765432040. Rollout percentage increased from 10% -> 100% over ~2m. Automated checks passed during canary window.

sanjay (frontend): repro: hitting /v1/generate with same prompt gets 504s intermittently. local curl shows repeated `504 Gateway Timeout` and sometimes `upstream read timeout`. sample curl: ```curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'``` logs show long tail waiting on runtime KV lookup.

luca (runtime): checking runtime. I'm seeing a sharp increase in kv-cache miss latency and connection resets to backend model-workers. kvcache eviction spikes coincide with canary promotion. suspect new model variant triggers larger reqs (longer seqs) and causes memory pressure + GC/evictions. tail from runtime logs: ```[13:34:02] WARN kv_cache: evicting 42 entries (mem high)
[13:34:03] ERROR worker_conn: reset by peer (id=worker-72)```.

emma (oncall-sre): thanks. sounds like deploy changed behavior that increases kv footprint -> cascading stalls. We need immediate mitigation: 1) stop rollout (if still ongoing), 2) revert to previous model/commit, 3) divert traffic to fallback model or region if revert takes >2m, 4) communicate customer impact. @sanjay can you open a rollback?

sanjay (frontend): initiating rollback now. command: ```./infra/rollout rollback dep-20260315-1315 --force --reason "timeout regression p99"```.

prod-alerts-bot: Rollback job started (job_id=rb-4765432110). Notifying load balancers to pin traffic to prior variant.

luca (runtime): quick mitigation we can also do: reduce max sequence length cap at the router to prevent oversized requests hitting the new model variant; also increase kv cache size if infra allows. I'll open a short-lived override: `KV_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES=20000` for eu-west-1. applying now.

maya (support): logging customer impact: initial alert shows 1.2% of paying customers saw >=1 error in the last 5m. Top affected tenants: corp-ops (10% of their requests), edu-sync (6%). Opening a customer-impact ticket and notifying CSMs.

emma (oncall-sre): rollback progress? any telemetry?

sanjay (frontend): rb job finished: status=success at 4765432132. Promoted previous variant back to 100%. deploy-bot confirms previous model pinned.

prod-alerts-bot: Post-rollback metrics (30s window): p95=230ms, p99=450ms, 5xx rate=0.12%. Starting to trend back to baseline.

luca (runtime): KV override helped dampen the tail during the rollback but we still saw several worker reconnects. I'll keep the KV_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES override for 10m and also disable a new kernel optimization that the new variant enabled; that optimization seems to increase memory mapping churn. Patch command: `runtimectl set-flag disable_new_kern_opt=true --region eu-west-1`. Applying.

emma (oncall-sre): good. @maya start a brief customer notification: incident affecting a subset of requests in eu-west-1 between 13:34-13:32? (typo) — correct window 13:34-13:33 UTC? let's be precise: root cause window 4765432100 (13:33:20 UTC) -> rollback at 4765432132 (13:35:32 UTC). Keep it short: "We've mitigated a service disruption caused by a recent deploy; a subset of requests experienced elevated timeouts/502s between 13:33‑13:35 UTC, now resolved."

maya (support): drafting notification and posting to status page. also creating CS tickets for corp-ops and edu-sync. will include any temporary workarounds (retry/backoff guidance).

sanjay (frontend): running smoke tests against a few tenants now. sample result: 100/100 requests succeeded to /v1/generate with expected latency. no more 504s in last 90s.

emma (oncall-sre): ok stabilizing. action items before handoff: - create an incident short doc (what changed, metrics, rollback timeline) - assign runtime owner to root cause (luca) - follow up with model team to check model variant config that increased KV footprint - perf test new variant on staging with kv stress test before re-promote - schedule postmortem. I'll hand off to derek for the rest of the night.

derek (shift-lead): taking over. thanks @emma and team. I'll monitor eu-west-1 for 1hr and ensure follow-up tasks are created. @luca please post a timeline + logs into the postmortem. @sanjay please coordinate with model team before any re-rollouts.

prod-alerts-bot: final metrics snapshot: p95=200ms, p99=420ms, 5xx=0.08% (5m aggregate). Incident marked mitigated at 4765432140.

emma (oncall-sre): adding priority label P1->P2 after stabilization. will attach traces and example request ids. good job everyone. :white_check_mark: 

maya (support): status page updated, customers notified.

luca (runtime): quick note for postmortem: please collect heap/kv histograms from worker-70..75 around 13:32-13:36 and the model metadata for the promoted variant (model_id=m-20260315-v2-large). I'll dump configs to the incident doc.

sanjay (frontend): created postmortem issue: https://redwood-internal/infra/incidents/4765432100 - assigning to runtime + model teams.

derek (shift-lead): handoff completed. monitoring window started. I'll escalate if anything re-surges.

emma (oncall-sre): closing handoff. thanks all. :pray:
